compositeLabelProhibition: EVENT_SPIKE and UNKNOWN are not outcomes in the same probability simplex as LOW/NORMAL/HIGH. Event attribution and evidence sufficiency remain separate axes.
classificationUnit: local market cell × accommodation type × individual stay night × lead-time context
aggregationRules: Classify each consumed night from check-in through the day before check-out.
Aggregate price and availability axes separately; a stay with different known nightly states is MIXED on that axis only.
Any material night without sufficient local evidence makes the affected stay axis UNKNOWN.
INDETERMINATE is required for event attribution when identification or provenance is insufficient.
Event existence alone does not prove ATTRIBUTED impact; a local counterfactual and uncertainty are required.
prohibitedInferences: No citywide month label is a universal local-season truth.
No fixed global percentile or price threshold defines a low or high local price regime.
No composite EVENT_SPIKE probability may mix causal attribution with price state or evidence sufficiency.
Local market context is not a numeric ranking contribution.
A high-season price is not automatically good value and a low-season price is not automatically a deal.
A sold-out-evidenced property is censored market evidence, not a zero-price or ignorable observation.
An unavailable or absent result is not sold out unless the reason is explicitly evidenced.
No universal book-now, wait or book-early rule may be emitted without calibrated historical paths.
